vue-dnd-kit.title: Vue DnD Kit
vue-dnd-kit.summary: Headless drag-and-drop for Vue 3 and TypeScript: attaches to any element through a template ref, with no markup forced on you.
vue-dnd-kit.challenge: Drag and drop in real products is more than moving a card: nested zones, trees and kanban boards, multi-drag, auto-scroll, keyboard access and syncing with the backend.
vue-dnd-kit.solution: A composable API — makeDraggable and makeDroppable — adds dragging to any element through a template ref. Async drops (onDrop returns a Promise), keyboard navigation, and a zero-dependency monorepo (core + utilities) with full typing and tree-shaking. Docs with interactive examples live on GitHub Pages.

wispbringer.title: Wispbringer
wispbringer.summary: A survivors-like on my own engine: rendered with Three.js, every visual effect is a custom GLSL shader.
wispbringer.challenge: A game on a home-made engine instead of an off-the-shelf framework: rendering, effects and the asset pipeline are all my own.
wispbringer.solution: Rendering on Three.js, every effect a custom GLSL shader. Assets are cut automatically with SpriteCutter. The demo is playable; a desktop port and a Steam release are in progress.

spritecutter.title: SpriteCutter
spritecutter.summary: Cuts sprite sheets automatically — including AI-generated ones, where standard algorithms get it wrong.
spritecutter.challenge: On AI-generated sheets sprites sit off-centre and packed tight, so standard algorithms cut them wrong — and doing one sheet by hand in Photoshop takes about five minutes.
spritecutter.solution: A custom detection algorithm copes with the offsets and the tight packing. Odd sheets get a manual mode, plus animation export and batch renaming by template with similarity matching. One sheet now takes about a minute.

engine.title: Game engine
engine.summary: An editor that builds browser games for web and desktop — with a built-in AI agent that knows the engine’s API.
facts: AI agent that knows the API
engine.challenge: A comfortable editor where a browser game comes together for both web and desktop — and an assistant that helps put it together.
engine.solution: A desktop app on Electron + Nuxt + Vue 3, UI on shadcn-vue, state in Pinia and VueUse. The built-in AI agent knows the engine’s API and helps assemble the game right inside the editor. The project is closed, so no links yet.

about.titleAfter: so nothing gets lost between the mockup and the code.
about.text: For seven years I’ve been designing and building complex interfaces: e-commerce with a 3D configurator across 50,000+ products, visual editors, drag-and-drop systems, real-time WebSocket dashboards, CRMs and SSO. I make architecture calls, build reusable component foundations, hire and mentor developers — and work with AI tools: Cursor, Claude Code, MCP and my own skills.
